questions.stem:
Gram Co. develops computer programs to meet customers' special requirements. How should Gram categorize payments to employees who develop these programs?
Direct costs | Value-adding costs
questions.explanation: The programmers work on specific customer programs, so their pay can be traced to those jobs and is a direct cost. Writing the software is also what the customer is paying for, so the activity adds value. Both answers are therefore yes.
questions.explanationJa: プログラマーは特定顧客向けのプログラムに従事しているため、その給与は個々のジョブに跡づけられ直接費となる。またソフトウェアを書く作業こそ顧客が対価を払っている対象なので、付加価値を生む活動でもある。したがって両方ともYesとなる。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to the August manufacturing activities of Griss Co.:
Beginning work-in-process | $12,000
Ending work-in-process | 10,000
Cost of goods manufactured | 97,000
Direct materials issued to production | 20,000
Factory overhead is assigned at 150 percent of direct labor. What was the August direct labor?
questions.explanation: Cost of goods manufactured = beginning WIP + materials + labor + overhead - ending WIP. Overhead is 150% of labor, so: $97,000 = $12,000 + $20,000 + L + 1.5L - $10,000. That gives 2.5L = $75,000 and L = $30,000. Treating overhead as a separate unknown is what makes this look harder than it is.
questions.explanationJa: 当期製品製造原価 = 期首仕掛品 + 直接材料 + 直接労務 + 製造間接費 − 期末仕掛品。間接費は労務費の150%なので、$97,000 = $12,000 + $20,000 + L + 1.5L − $10,000。整理すると 2.5L = $75,000、L = $30,000。間接費を別の未知数として扱おうとすると難しく見えるが、労務費の関数として置くのが要点。

questions.stem: Which of the following topics is the focus of managerial accounting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Financial statements and other financial reports

choices.label: D
choices.text: The needs of the organization's internal parties

questions.explanation: Managerial accounting exists to support decisions made inside the organization, so it is free of the constraints that govern external reporting. Financial statements, historical cost and creditor needs all describe financial accounting, which serves outside users.
questions.explanationJa: 管理会計は組織内部の意思決定を支えるために存在するので、外部報告を縛る制約を受けない。財務諸表、取得原価主義、債権者のニーズはいずれも外部利用者に向けた財務会計の説明である。

questions.stem:
Day Mail Order Co. applied the high-low method of cost estimation to customer order data for the first 4 months of the year.
Month | Orders | Cost
January | 1,200 | $ 3,120
February | 1,300 | 3,185
March | 1,800 | 4,320
April | 1,700 | 3,895
6,000 | $14,520
What is the estimated variable order filling cost component per order?
questions.explanation: The high-low method uses only the highest and lowest ACTIVITY levels: March at 1,800 orders and January at 1,200. Variable rate = ($4,320 - $3,120) / (1,800 - 1,200) = $1,200 / 600 = $2.00 per order. Note the high month is chosen by order volume, not by cost.
questions.explanationJa: 高低点法は最高と最低の「操業度」だけを使う。最高は3月の1,800件、最低は1月の1,200件。変動費率 = ($4,320 − $3,120) ÷ (1,800 − 1,200) = $1,200 ÷ 600 = $2.00/件。基準にするのは金額ではなく件数である点に注意する。

questions.stem:
In the budgeted profit-volume chart below, EG represents a two-product company's profit path. EH and HG represent the profit paths of products #1 and #2, respectively.
Sales prices and cost behavior were as budgeted, actual total sales equaled budgeted sales, and there were no inventories. Actual profit was greater than budgeted profit. Which product had actual sales in excess of budget, and what margin does OE divided by OF represent?
Product with excess | OE/OF
sales

figure.alt: Budgeted profit-volume chart. The solid line EG is the two-product profit path, crossing the volume axis at F. The dashed path E-H-G shows product #1 from E to H and product #2 from H to G.

questions.explanation: On a profit-volume chart the slope of each line is the contribution margin ratio, since profit rises by the contribution margin on each additional sales dollar. With total sales on budget but profit above budget, the mix must have shifted toward the steeper line, which is product #1. The ratio OE/OF measures that slope and is therefore the contribution margin.
questions.explanationJa: 利益図表では各線の傾きが貢献利益率を表す。売上が1ドル増えるごとに利益は貢献利益の分だけ増えるためである。売上合計は予算どおりで利益だけが予算を上回ったのだから、構成が傾きの急な線、すなわち製品#1の側へ移ったことになる。OE ÷ OF はその傾きを測る比率なので貢献利益率にあたる。

questions.stem:
The following information is available on Crain Co.'s two product lines:
Chairs | Tables
Sales | $180,000 | $48,000
Variable costs | (96,000) | (30,000)
Contribution margin | 84,000 | 18,000
Fixed costs:
Avoidable | (36,000) | (12,000)
Unavoidable | (18,000) | (10,800)
Operating income (loss) | $30,000 | $(4,800)
Assuming the tables line is discontinued, and the factory space previously used to make tables is rented for $24,000 per year, operating income will increase by what amount?
questions.explanation: Dropping tables loses their $18,000 contribution margin but saves the $12,000 of avoidable fixed costs and brings in $24,000 of rent. Net change = -$18,000 + $12,000 + $24,000 = $18,000 increase. The $10,800 of unavoidable fixed costs continues either way and must be left out.
questions.explanationJa: テーブルを廃止すると貢献利益 $18,000 を失うが、回避可能固定費 $12,000 が節約でき、賃貸収入 $24,000 が入る。純変化 = −$18,000 + $12,000 + $24,000 = $18,000 の増加。回避不能固定費 $10,800 はどちらにせよ発生し続けるため、計算に含めてはならない。

questions.stem:
The diagram below is a cost-volume-profit chart.
At point A compared to point B, as a percentage of sales revenues
Variable costs are | Fixed costs are

figure.alt: Cost-volume-profit chart. A steep total revenue line from the origin crosses a flatter total cost line, with a horizontal line marking fixed costs. Points A and B lie on the total cost line, A at a lower activity level than B.

questions.explanation: Variable cost is a constant proportion of each sales dollar, so as a percentage of revenue it is the same at any volume. Total fixed cost does not change with volume, so spreading it over smaller revenue makes it a larger percentage. At the lower-volume point the fixed cost percentage is therefore greater.
questions.explanationJa: 変動費は売上1ドルに対して常に一定の割合を占めるため、売上に対する比率はどの操業度でも変わらない。固定費の総額は操業度によって変化しないので、売上が小さいほど売上に占める割合は大きくなる。したがって操業度の低い点では固定費の比率の方が大きい。

questions.stem:
The following information data pertains to a manufacturing company:
Total sales | $80,000
Total variable costs | 20,000
Total fixed costs | 30,000
What is the break-even level in sales dollars?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin ratio = ($80,000 - $20,000) / $80,000 = 75%. Break-even sales = fixed costs / contribution margin ratio = $30,000 / 0.75 = $40,000. Answering $30,000 confuses the fixed cost itself with the sales needed to cover it.
questions.explanationJa: 貢献利益率 = ($80,000 − $20,000) ÷ $80,000 = 75%。損益分岐点売上高 = 固定費 ÷ 貢献利益率 = $30,000 ÷ 0.75 = $40,000。$30,000 と答えるのは、固定費そのものと、それを回収するのに必要な売上高とを取り違えている。

questions.stem: Cuff Caterers quotes a price of $60 per person for a dinner party. This price includes the 6% sales tax and the 15% service charge. Sales tax is computed on the food plus the service charge. The service charge is computed on the food only. At what amount does Cuff price the food?
questions.explanation: Build the price up from the food. Service charge is 15% of food, and sales tax is 6% of food plus service charge: $60 = F + 0.15F + 0.06(1.15F) = F(1 + 0.15 + 0.069) = 1.219F. So F = $60 / 1.219 = $49.22. Applying both percentages to the $60 quoted price would work backwards from the wrong base.
questions.explanationJa: 食事代を起点に価格を積み上げる。サービス料は食事代の15%、売上税は食事代とサービス料の合計の6%なので、$60 = F + 0.15F + 0.06(1.15F) = F(1 + 0.15 + 0.069) = 1.219F。よって F = $60 ÷ 1.219 = $49.22。提示価格 $60 に各率を直接掛けると、誤った基礎額から逆算することになる。

questions.stem: A company produces and sells two products. The first product accounts for 75% of sales and the second product accounts for the remaining 25% of sales. The first product has a selling price of $10 per unit, variable costs of $6 per unit, and allocated fixed costs of $100,000. The second product has a selling price of $25 per unit, variable costs of $13 per unit, and allocated fixed costs of $212,000. At the break- even point, what number of units of the first product will have been sold?
questions.explanation: The 75/25 split is by units. Let total units = Q. Weighted contribution margin = 0.75 x $4 + 0.25 x $12 = $3 + $3 = $6 per unit. Total fixed costs = $100,000 + $212,000 = $312,000, so Q = $312,000 / $6 = 52,000 units. The first product accounts for 75% = 39,000 units.

questions.stem:
Big Corporation currently operates two divisions that had operating results for calendar Year 1, as follows:
West Division | East Division
Sales | $900,000 | $300,000
Variable costs | (510,000) | (230,000)
Contribution margin | 390,000 | 70,000
Fixed costs for the division | (110,000) | (50,000)
Margin over direct costs | 280,000 | 20,000
Allocated corporate costs | (135,000) | (45,000)
Operating income (loss) | $145,000 | $(25,000)
Since the East Division also sustained an operating loss during Year 0, Big's president is considering the elimination of this division. The East Division fixed costs could be avoided if the division was eliminated.
If the East Division had been eliminated on January 1, Year 1, Big Corporation's Year 1 operating income would have been
questions.explanation: Eliminating East loses its $70,000 contribution margin but saves the $50,000 of divisional fixed costs, a net loss of $20,000. The $45,000 of allocated corporate costs does not disappear; it is merely reassigned to West. The reported $25,000 loss is therefore misleading as a basis for the decision.
questions.explanationJa: East部門を廃止すると貢献利益 $70,000 を失う一方、部門固定費 $50,000 が節約でき、差引 $20,000 の減少となる。配賦された本社費 $45,000 は消えるわけではなく、West部門へ振り替わるだけである。したがって報告上の $25,000 の損失は、廃止の判断材料としては誤解を招く数値といえる。

questions.stem:
At annual sales of $900,000, the Ebo product has the following unit sales price and costs:
Sales price | $20
Prime cost | 6
Manufacturing overhead
- Variable | 1
- Fixed | 7
Selling & admin. costs
- Variable | 1
- Fixed | 3
18
Profit | $2
What is Ebo's breakeven point in units?
questions.explanation: Variable cost per unit = prime $6 + variable overhead $1 + variable selling $1 = $8, so contribution margin = $20 - $8 = $12. Units currently sold = $900,000 / $20 = 45,000, and fixed cost per unit is $7 + $3 = $10, so total fixed cost = 45,000 x $10 = $450,000. Break-even = $450,000 / $12 = 37,500 units.

questions.stem:
Product Cott has sales of $200,000, a contribution margin of 20%, and a margin of safety of $80,000.
What is Cott's fixed cost?
questions.explanation: Margin of safety is sales above break-even, so break-even sales = $200,000 - $80,000 = $120,000. At break-even, contribution margin exactly covers fixed cost: $120,000 x 20% = $24,000. Applying the 20% to the margin of safety instead gives $16,000.
questions.explanationJa: 安全余裕は損益分岐点を上回る売上高なので、損益分岐点売上高 = $200,000 − $80,000 = $120,000。損益分岐点では貢献利益が固定費とちょうど一致するので、固定費 = $120,000 × 20% = $24,000。20%を安全余裕の方に掛けると $16,000 となり誤る。

questions.stem:
Based on potential sales of 500 units per year, a new product has estimated traceable costs of $990,000.
What is the target price to obtain a 15% profit margin on sales?
questions.explanation: A 15% margin ON SALES means profit is 15% of price, not of cost. Cost per unit = $990,000 / 500 = $1,980, and price - $1,980 = 0.15 x price, so 0.85 x price = $1,980 and price = $2,329. Marking cost up by 15% would give $2,277, which is the margin on cost rather than on sales.
questions.explanationJa: 「売上に対する」15%の利益率とは、利益が原価ではなく価格の15%であることを意味する。単位原価 = $990,000 ÷ 500 = $1,980 として、価格 − $1,980 = 0.15 × 価格。整理すると 0.85 × 価格 = $1,980、価格 = $2,329。原価に15%上乗せすると $2,277 となるが、それは売上ではなく原価に対する利益率である。

questions.stem: Carter Co. paid $1,000,000 for land three years ago. Carter estimates it can sell the land for $1,200,000, net of selling costs. If the land is not sold, Carter plans to develop the land at a cost of $1,500,000. Carter estimates net cash flow from the development in the first year of operations would be $500,000. What is Carter's opportunity cost of the development?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the benefit given up by choosing one course over the next best alternative. Developing the land means forgoing the $1,200,000 sale, so that is the opportunity cost. The $1,000,000 paid three years ago is a sunk cost, and the $1,500,000 development outlay is an out-of-pocket cost rather than a forgone benefit.
questions.explanationJa: 機会費用とは、ある選択をすることで放棄する次善の代替案の便益である。土地を開発するということは $1,200,000 での売却を諦めることなので、これが機会費用にあたる。3年前に支払った $1,000,000 は埋没原価であり、開発費 $1,500,000 は実際に支出する費用であって放棄する便益ではない。

questions.stem: Jackson Co. is considering a project that will use 2,000 square feet of storage space at one of its facilities to store used equipment. What will determine Jackson's opportunity cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The net present value of the project

choices.label: B
choices.text: The internal rate of return of the project

choices.label: C
choices.text: The value of the next best use of the space

choices.label: D
choices.text: The depreciation expense on the space

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is measured by what the resource would have earned in its next best use. If the storage space could have been rented or used for another project, that forgone benefit is the cost of devoting it to this one. Depreciation is a sunk allocation and the project's own NPV or IRR are outputs of the analysis, not inputs.
questions.explanationJa: 機会費用は、その資源を次善の用途に使った場合に得られたはずの価値で測る。この保管スペースを賃貸に出せた、あるいは別の案件に使えたのであれば、その放棄した便益が本件に充てることの費用となる。減価償却は既に確定した配賦額であり、当該案件のNPVやIRRは分析の結果であって入力値ではない。

questions.stem: When only differential manufacturing costs are taken into account for special order pricing, an essential assumption is that

choices.label: A
choices.text: Manufacturing fixed and variable costs are linear.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selling and administrative fixed and variable costs are linear.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acceptance of the order will not affect regular sales.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acceptance of the order will not cause unit selling and administrative variable costs to increase.

questions.explanation: Pricing on differential cost alone assumes the order adds business without displacing anything. If accepting it would cut into regular sales, the lost contribution margin on those sales becomes an opportunity cost that must be added, and the differential cost floor would be too low.
questions.explanationJa: 差額原価だけで価格を決められるのは、その注文が既存の取引を押しのけず純粋に上乗せとなる場合である。受注によって通常の販売が減るなら、失われる貢献利益が機会費用として加算されなければならず、差額原価だけの下限価格では低すぎることになる。

questions.stem:
Clay Co. has considerable excess manufacturing capacity. A special job order's cost sheet includes the following applied manufacturing overhead costs:
Fixed costs | $21,000
Variable costs | 33,000
The fixed costs include a normal $3,700 allocation for in-house design costs, although no in- house design will be done. Instead the job will require the use of external designers costing $7,750. What is the total amount to be included in the calculation to determine the minimum acceptable price for the job?
questions.explanation: With excess capacity the applied fixed overhead of $21,000 will be incurred regardless and is not relevant. What is relevant is the $33,000 of variable cost plus the $7,750 actually paid to external designers. The $3,700 in-house design allocation is removed because that work will not be done. Total = $40,750.
questions.explanationJa: 遊休能力があるため、配賦された固定費 $21,000 は受注の有無にかかわらず発生し、判断には関係しない。関連するのは変動費 $33,000 と、実際に支払う外部デザイナー費用 $7,750 である。社内デザイン費の配賦 $3,700 はその作業が行われないので除外する。合計 $40,750。

questions.stem:
Golden Inc., has been manufacturing 5,000 units of Part 10541 which is used in the manufacture of one of its products. At this level of production, the cost per unit of manufacturing Part 10541 is as follows:
Direct materials | $ 2
Direct labor | 8
Variable overhead | 4
Fixed overhead applied | 6
Total | $20
Brown Company has offered to sell Golden 5,000 units of Part 10541 for $19 a unit. Golden has determined that it could use the facilities presently used to manufacture Part 10541 to manufacture Product RAC and gener-ate an operating profit of $4,000. Golden has also determined that two-thirds of the fixed overhead applied will continue even if Part 10541 is purchased from Brown.
In deciding whether to make or buy that part, the total relevant costs to make the part are
questions.explanation: Relevant costs to make are those avoided by buying. All variable costs qualify: ($2 + $8 + $4) x 5,000 = $70,000. Only one-third of the fixed overhead disappears, so $6 x 1/3 x 5,000 = $10,000 is relevant while the other two-thirds continues either way. Total = $80,000.
questions.explanationJa: 自製の関連原価とは、購入すれば回避できる原価である。変動費はすべて該当する: ($2 + $8 + $4) × 5,000 = $70,000。固定費は3分の1しか消えないため、$6 × 1/3 × 5,000 = $10,000 が関連原価であり、残りの3分の2はどちらを選んでも発生し続ける。合計 $80,000。

questions.stem:
Golden Inc., has been manufacturing 5,000 units of Part 10541 which is used in the manufacture of one of its products. At this level of production, the cost per unit of manufacturing Part 10541 is as follows:
Direct materials | $ 2
Direct labor | 8
Variable overhead | 4
Fixed overhead applied | 6
Total | $20
Brown Company has offered to sell Golden 5,000 units of Part 10541 for $19 a unit. Golden has determined that it could use the facilities presently used to manufacture Part 10541 to manufacture Product RAC and gener-ate an operating profit of $4,000. Golden has also determined that two-thirds of the fixed overhead applied will continue even if Part 10541 is purchased from Brown.
Should Golden accept Brown's offer, and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No, because it would be $11,000 cheaper to make the part

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, because it would be $15,000 cheaper to make the part

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, because it would be $5,000 cheaper to buy the part

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, because it would be $9,000 cheaper to buy the part

questions.explanation: Cost to make = $80,000. Cost to buy = 5,000 x $19 = $95,000, but buying frees the facilities to earn $4,000 from Product RAC, so the net cost of buying is $91,000. Making is $91,000 - $80,000 = $11,000 cheaper, so the offer should be declined. Omitting the RAC profit would make the gap look like $15,000.
questions.explanationJa: 自製の原価 = $80,000。購入の原価 = 5,000 × $19 = $95,000 だが、購入すれば設備が空いて製品RACから $4,000 を稼げるため、購入の正味原価は $91,000。自製の方が $91,000 − $80,000 = $11,000 安いので、申し出は断るべきである。RACの利益を考慮しないと差は $15,000 に見えてしまう。

questions.stem: Gandy Company has 5,000 obsolete desk lamps that are carried in inventory at a manufacturing cost of $50,000. If the lamps are reworked for $20,000, they could be sold for $35,000. Alternatively, the lamps could be sold for $8,000 to a jobber located in a distant city. What alternative is more desirable and what are the total relevant costs for that alternative?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neither, since there is an overall loss under either alternative

questions.explanation: The $50,000 already in inventory is sunk and identical under both options, so it is excluded. Rework nets $35,000 - $20,000 = $15,000, while scrapping nets $8,000, so rework is better. The relevant cost of that alternative is only the $20,000 of additional work.
questions.explanationJa: 既に在庫に計上されている $50,000 は埋没原価であり、どちらを選んでも同じなので除外する。手直しは $35,000 − $20,000 = $15,000 の正味収入、スクラップ売却は $8,000 なので手直しが有利。その代替案の関連原価は追加で要する $20,000 だけである。

questions.stem:
A company's controller is adjusting next year's budget to reflect to the impact of an expected 5% inflation rate. Listed below are selected items from next year's budget before the adjustment:
Total salaries expense | $250,000
Health costs | 100,000
Depreciation expense | 65,000
Interest expense on 10-year fixed-rate note | 37,750
After adjusting for the 5% inflation rate, what is the company's total budget for the selected items before taxes for next year?
questions.explanation: Inflation raises costs that are repriced each period: salaries $250,000 x 1.05 = $262,500 and health costs $100,000 x 1.05 = $105,000. Depreciation is based on historical cost and interest on a fixed-rate note is contractually set, so neither changes. Total = $262,500 + $105,000 + $65,000 + $37,750 = $470,250.
questions.explanationJa: インフレの影響を受けるのは毎期価格が改定される費用である。給与 $250,000 × 1.05 = $262,500、医療費 $100,000 × 1.05 = $105,000。減価償却費は取得原価に基づき、固定金利の利息は契約で定まっているため、いずれも変動しない。合計 = $262,500 + $105,000 + $65,000 + $37,750 = $470,250。

questions.stem: A company is offered a one-time special order for its product has the capacity to make this order with- out losing current business. Variable costs per unit and fixed costs in total will be the same. The gross profit for the special order will be 10%, which is 15% less than the usual gross profit. What impact will this order have on total fixed costs and operating income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Total fixed costs increase, and operating income increases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Total fixed costs do not change, and operating income increases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Total fixed costs do not change, and operating income does not change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Total fixed costs increase, and operating income decreases.

questions.explanation: The order is filled with existing capacity, so total fixed costs are unchanged. A 10% gross profit still means revenue exceeds the incremental cost, so the contribution flows straight to operating income. A lower-than-usual margin does not make an order unprofitable when the fixed costs are already covered by regular business.
questions.explanationJa: 既存の能力の範囲で受注をこなすため、固定費総額は変わらない。売上総利益率が10%であっても収益は増分原価を上回っているので、その貢献分はそのまま営業利益に加わる。固定費が通常の事業で既に回収されている以上、利益率が普段より低いことは受注が不採算であることを意味しない。

questions.stem: Spring Co. had two divisions, A and B. Division A created Product X, which could be sold on the outside market for $25 and used variable costs of $15. Division B could take Product X and apply additional variable costs of $40 to create Product Y, which could be sold for $100. Division B received a special order for a large amount of Product Y. If Division A were operating at full capacity, which of the following prices should Division A charge Division B for the Product X needed to fill the special order?
questions.explanation: At full capacity, every unit transferred internally is a unit not sold outside, so Division A gives up the $25 market price. The transfer price must cover the $15 variable cost plus the $10 contribution forgone, which equals the market price of $25. At less than full capacity the floor would be only the $15 variable cost.
questions.explanationJa: フル操業下では、社内へ振り替える1単位は外部へ売れない1単位を意味するため、A部門は市場価格 $25 を放棄することになる。振替価格は変動費 $15 に、放棄する貢献利益 $10 を加えた額、すなわち市場価格 $25 でなければならない。フル操業でなければ下限は変動費 $15 で足りる。

questions.stem:
Vince Inc. has developed and patented a new laser disc reading device that will be marketed internationally. Which of the following factors should Vince consider in pricing the device?
I. Quality of the new device
II. Life of the new device III. Customers' relative preference for quality compared to price
questions.explanation: Pricing a new patented product requires judging what the market will bear, which depends on the quality offered, how long the device will remain useful and current before obsolescence, and how much customers value quality relative to price. All three shape the demand curve the company faces.
questions.explanationJa: 特許を取得した新製品の価格設定では、市場が受け入れる水準を見極める必要がある。それは提供する品質、陳腐化するまでどれだけ有用で先進的であり続けるかという製品寿命、そして顧客が価格に対して品質をどれだけ重視するかに左右される。3つとも企業が直面する需要曲線を形づくる要素である。

questions.stem:
In calculating the break-even point for a multi-product company, which of the following assumptions are commonly made when variable costing is used?
I. Sales volume equals production volume.
II. Variable costs are constant per unit.
III. A given sales mix is maintained for all volume changes.
questions.explanation: Break-even analysis assumes variable cost per unit stays constant and that the sales mix holds as volume changes, since a shifting mix would change the weighted contribution margin. Sales equalling production matters under absorption costing, where fixed overhead moves with inventory, but not under variable costing.
questions.explanationJa: 損益分岐点分析では、単位あたり変動費が一定であること、そして操業度が変わっても販売構成が保たれることを前提とする。構成が変われば加重平均貢献利益が変わってしまうためである。販売量と生産量が一致するという前提が必要なのは、固定費が在庫とともに動く全部原価計算の場合であって、直接原価計算では不要である。

questions.stem: Jago Co. has 2 products that use the same manufacturing facilities and cannot be subcontracted. Each product has sufficient orders to utilize the entire manufacturing capacity. For short-run profit maximization, Jago should manufacture the product with the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower total manufacturing costs for the manufacturing capacity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower total variable manufacturing costs for the manufacturing capacity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greater gross profit per hour of manufacturing capacity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Greater contribution margin per hour of manufacturing capacity

questions.explanation: When capacity is the binding constraint, profit is maximised by earning the most contribution from each unit of that constraint, so the product with the greater contribution margin per hour wins. Gross profit per hour is distorted by allocated fixed overhead, which does not change with the choice.
questions.explanationJa: 生産能力が制約となる場合、その制約1単位あたりで最も多くの貢献利益を稼ぐことで利益が最大化されるため、時間あたり貢献利益の大きい製品を選ぶ。時間あたり売上総利益は配賦された固定費に歪められており、その固定費はどちらを選んでも変わらない。

questions.stem:
Using the variable costing method, which of the following costs are assigned to inventory?
Variable selling and | Variable factory
administrative costs | overhead costs
questions.explanation: Variable costing inventories only the variable costs of manufacturing, so variable factory overhead is included. Selling and administrative costs are period costs whether variable or fixed, because they are not incurred to produce the goods.
questions.explanationJa: 直接原価計算では製造にかかる変動費だけを棚卸資産に含めるため、変動製造間接費は算入される。販売費及び一般管理費は、変動費であれ固定費であれ期間費用として処理する。製品を製造するために発生する費用ではないからである。

questions.stem: In an income statement prepared as an internal report using the variable costing method, variable selling and administrative expenses would

choices.label: B
choices.text: Be used in the computation of operating income but not in the computation of the contribution margin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Be treated the same as fixed selling and administrative expenses

choices.label: D
choices.text: Be used in the computation of the contribution margin

questions.explanation: Variable costing separates costs by behaviour, not by function, so contribution margin is sales less ALL variable costs, including variable selling and administrative expenses. Only the fixed portion is deducted afterwards to arrive at operating income.
questions.explanationJa: 直接原価計算は費用を機能別ではなく変動・固定の別で区分するため、貢献利益は売上からすべての変動費を差し引いて求める。変動販売費及び一般管理費もここに含まれる。固定費部分は貢献利益の後で控除し、営業利益に至る。

questions.stem:
Selected information concerning the operations of a company for the year ended December 31 is as follows:
Units produced | 20,000
Units sold | 18,000
Direct materials used | 80,000
Direct labor incurred | $40,000
Fixed factory overhead | $50,000
Variable factory overhead | $24,000
Fixed selling and administrative expenses | $60,000
Variable selling and administrative expenses | $ 9,000
Work-in-process inventories at the beginning and end of the year were zero. What was the company's finished goods inventory cost at December 31 under the variable (direct) costing method?
questions.explanation: Variable costing inventories only variable manufacturing costs: $80,000 materials + $40,000 labor + $24,000 variable overhead = $144,000 for 20,000 units, or $7.20 each. Ending inventory = 20,000 - 18,000 = 2,000 units x $7.20 = $14,400. Fixed factory overhead and all selling costs are expensed as incurred.
questions.explanationJa: 直接原価計算では変動製造原価だけを棚卸資産に含める: 材料 $80,000 + 労務 $40,000 + 変動製造間接費 $24,000 = $144,000 を 20,000単位で割ると 1単位 $7.20。期末在庫 = 20,000 − 18,000 = 2,000単位 × $7.20 = $14,400。固定製造間接費と販管費はすべて発生時に費用処理する。

questions.stem: A direct labor overtime premium should be charged to a specific job when the overtime is caused by the

choices.label: B
choices.text: Customer's requirement for early completion of job

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management's failure to include the job in the production schedule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Management's requirement that the job be completed before the annual factory vacation closure

questions.explanation: An overtime premium belongs to a specific job only when that job is the reason the overtime occurred, as when a customer demands early completion. If overtime stems from general busyness or from scheduling failures, it is a cost of operations as a whole and goes to factory overhead so it is spread across all jobs.
questions.explanationJa: 残業割増を特定のジョブに賦課してよいのは、そのジョブ自体が残業の原因である場合に限られる。顧客が早期完成を要求した場合がこれにあたる。全体的な繁忙や生産計画の不備から生じた残業は事業全体の費用であり、製造間接費として全ジョブに配賦する。

questions.stem:
The following is selected information from the records of Ray, Inc.:
Purchases of raw materials | $ 6,000
Raw materials, beginning | 500
Raw materials, ending | 800
Work-in-process, beginning | 0
Work-in-process, ending | 0
Cost of goods sold | 12,000
Finished goods, beginning | 1,200
Finished goods, ending | 1,400
What is the total amount of conversion, costs?
questions.explanation: Materials used = $500 + $6,000 - $800 = $5,700. Cost of goods manufactured = cost of goods sold $12,000 + ending finished goods $1,400 - beginning $1,200 = $12,200, which equals total manufacturing cost since work-in-process is zero at both ends. Conversion cost = $12,200 - $5,700 = $6,500.
questions.explanationJa: 材料消費額 = $500 + $6,000 − $800 = $5,700。当期製品製造原価 = 売上原価 $12,000 + 期末製品 $1,400 − 期首製品 $1,200 = $12,200。仕掛品が期首・期末ともゼロなので、これが当期総製造費用に等しい。加工費 = $12,200 − $5,700 = $6,500。

questions.stem:
Following are Mill Co.'s production costs for October:
Direct materials | $100,000
Direct labor | 90,000
Factory overhead | 4,000
What amount of costs should be traced to specific products in the production process?
questions.explanation: Costs traced to specific products are those that can be followed directly to a unit: direct materials $100,000 plus direct labor $90,000 = $190,000. Factory overhead is by definition indirect and must be allocated rather than traced.
questions.explanationJa: 特定の製品に跡づけられる原価とは、個々の製品まで直接たどれる原価であり、直接材料 $100,000 と直接労務 $90,000 の合計 $190,000 がこれにあたる。製造間接費は定義上、間接費であり、跡づけではなく配賦によって割り当てる。

questions.stem:
What is the cost of ending inventory given the following factors?
Beginning inventory | $ 5,000
Total production costs | 60,000
Cost of goods sold | 55,000
Direct labor | 40,000
questions.explanation: Ending inventory = beginning inventory + costs added - cost of goods sold = $5,000 + $60,000 - $55,000 = $10,000. Direct labor of $40,000 is already inside the $60,000 of total production costs, so adding it separately would double count.
questions.explanationJa: 期末在庫 = 期首在庫 + 当期投入原価 − 売上原価 = $5,000 + $60,000 − $55,000 = $10,000。直接労務費 $40,000 は総製造費用 $60,000 に既に含まれているため、別途加算すると二重計上になる。

questions.stem:
Fab Co. manufactures textiles. Among Fab's June manufacturing costs were the following salaries and wages:
Loom operators | $120,000
Factory foremen | 45,000
Machine mechanics | 30,000
What was the amount of Fab's June direct labor?
questions.explanation: Direct labor is the wages of workers who physically convert materials into product, which here is the loom operators at $120,000. Foremen supervise rather than operate, and mechanics maintain equipment, so both are indirect labor charged to factory overhead.
questions.explanationJa: 直接労務費は、材料を製品へと実際に加工する作業者の賃金であり、ここでは織機オペレーターの $120,000 が該当する。職長は監督業務、整備工は設備の保守を担うため、いずれも間接労務費として製造間接費に集計される。

questions.stem: Which of the following is assigned to goods that were either purchased or manufactured for resale?
questions.explanation: Product costs attach to goods bought or made for resale and stay in inventory until the goods are sold, at which point they become cost of goods sold. Period costs are expensed as incurred regardless of sales, and relevant and opportunity costs are decision-making concepts rather than inventory classifications.
questions.explanationJa: 製品原価は再販売のために購入または製造した財に付随し、その財が販売されるまで棚卸資産に留まり、販売時に売上原価となる。期間費用は販売の有無にかかわらず発生時に費用処理される。関連原価や機会費用は意思決定のための概念であり、棚卸資産の分類ではない。

questions.stem: In job cost systems, is manufacturing overhead (1) an indirect cost of jobs, and (2) a necessary element in production?
questions.explanation: Manufacturing overhead cannot be traced to individual jobs, so it is an indirect cost and must be applied through a rate. It is nonetheless essential to production, since without power, supervision and facilities no job could be completed. Both statements are true.
questions.explanationJa: 製造間接費は個々のジョブに跡づけられないため間接費であり、配賦率を通じて割り当てる必要がある。しかし生産に不可欠であることに変わりはない。動力・監督・設備がなければどのジョブも完成しないからである。したがって両方の記述が正しい。

questions.stem:
Given that demand exceeds capacity, that there is no spoilage or waste, and that there is full utilization of a constant number of assembly hours, the number of components needed for an assembly operation with an 80 percent learning curve should
I. Increase for successive periods
II. Decrease per unit of output
questions.explanation: With a learning curve, each successive unit takes less assembly time, so a constant number of hours yields more units as workers gain experience. More units means more components are needed in later periods. The components required per unit of output do not change, since the learning affects labor time rather than material content.
questions.explanationJa: 学習曲線の下では後続の単位ほど組立時間が短くなるため、投入時間が一定でも習熟に伴って産出単位数は増える。産出が増えれば後の期ほど必要な部品数も増える。一方、産出1単位あたりに必要な部品数は変わらない。学習効果が及ぶのは作業時間であって材料の所要量ではないからである。

questions.stem:
Mat Co. estimated its material handling costs at two activity levels as follows:
Kilos handled | Cost
80,000 | $160,000
60,000 | $132,000
What is the estimated cost for handling 75,000 kilos?
questions.explanation: High-low method: variable rate = ($160,000 - $132,000) / (80,000 - 60,000) = $1.40 per kilo. Fixed cost = $160,000 - (80,000 x $1.40) = $48,000. Estimated cost at 75,000 kilos = $48,000 + (75,000 x $1.40) = $153,000. Simply scaling the $160,000 proportionally ignores the fixed component.

questions.stem:
Briar Co. signed a government construction contract providing for a formula price of actual cost plus 10%.
In addition, Briar was to receive one-half of any savings resulting from the formula price being less than the target price of $2,200,000. Briar's actual costs incurred were $1,920,000. How much should Briar receive from the contract?
Del Co. has fixed costs of $100,000 and break-even sales of $800,000. What is its projected profit at $1,200,000 sales?
questions.explanation: At break-even, contribution margin exactly equals fixed cost, so the contribution margin ratio = $100,000 / $800,000 = 12.5%. Every sales dollar beyond break-even adds that ratio to profit: ($1,200,000 - $800,000) x 12.5% = $50,000.
questions.explanationJa: 損益分岐点では貢献利益が固定費とちょうど一致するので、貢献利益率 = $100,000 ÷ $800,000 = 12.5%。損益分岐点を超えた売上はその率の分だけ利益に加わる: ($1,200,000 − $800,000) × 12.5% = $50,000。

questions.stem: The contribution margin ratio always increases when the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Variable costs as a percentage of net sales increase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Variable costs as a percentage of net sales decrease

questions.explanation: Contribution margin ratio = 1 - variable cost ratio, so the two always move in opposite directions. A falling break-even point is a consequence of a higher contribution margin ratio or lower fixed costs, not a cause, so it does not always accompany the change.
questions.explanationJa: 貢献利益率 = 1 − 変動費率であるから、両者は常に逆方向に動く。損益分岐点の低下は、貢献利益率の上昇か固定費の減少がもたらす「結果」であって原因ではないため、貢献利益率の上昇と必ず対応するわけではない。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Casa Co.'s cost-volume-profit relationships:
Break-even point in units sold | 1,000
Variable costs per unit | $ 500
Total fixed costs | $300,000
How much will be contributed to profit before income taxes by the 1,001st unit sold?
questions.explanation: At break-even, contribution margin exactly covers fixed cost, so contribution margin per unit = $300,000 / 1,000 = $300. Every unit beyond break-even adds its full contribution margin to profit, so the 1,001st unit contributes $300. The $500 variable cost is already deducted in arriving at that figure.
questions.explanationJa: 損益分岐点では貢献利益が固定費とちょうど一致するので、単位あたり貢献利益 = $300,000 ÷ 1,000単位 = $300。損益分岐点を超えた単位は、その貢献利益の全額が利益に加わるため、1,001単位目の貢献は $300 となる。変動費 $500 はこの金額を出す時点で既に差し引かれている。

questions.stem: Pinecrest Co. had variable costs of 25% of sales, and fixed costs of $30,000. Pinecrest's break-even point in sales dollars was
questions.explanation: If variable costs are 25% of sales, the contribution margin ratio is 75%. Break-even sales = fixed costs / contribution margin ratio = $30,000 / 0.75 = $40,000. Dividing by the 25% variable ratio instead would give $120,000.
questions.explanationJa: 変動費が売上の25%であれば、貢献利益率は75%となる。損益分岐点売上高 = 固定費 ÷ 貢献利益率 = $30,000 ÷ 0.75 = $40,000。変動費率25%で割ると $120,000 となり誤る。

questions.stem:
The following information is taken from Wampler Co.'s contribution income statement:
Sales | $200,000
Contribution margin | 120,000
Fixed costs | 90,000
Income taxes | 12,000
What was Wampler's margin of safety?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin ratio = $120,000 / $200,000 = 60%. Break-even sales = $90,000 / 0.60 = $150,000. Margin of safety = actual sales - break-even sales = $200,000 - $150,000 = $50,000. Income taxes do not enter the calculation.

questions.stem: At the break-even point, the contribution margin equals total
questions.explanation: Break-even is defined as the point where profit is zero, which happens when the contribution margin generated exactly absorbs total fixed costs. Sales revenue at that point equals variable plus fixed costs, not the contribution margin alone.
questions.explanationJa: 損益分岐点とは利益がゼロになる点であり、それは生み出された貢献利益が固定費の総額をちょうど吸収するときに成立する。その時点の売上高は変動費と固定費の合計に等しく、貢献利益そのものとは一致しない。

questions.stem: A company that produces 10,000 units has fixed costs of $300,000, variable costs of $50 per unit, and a sales price of $85 per unit. After learning that its variable costs will increase by 20%, the company is considering an increase in production to 12,000 units. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the company's next steps?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If production is increased to 12,000 units, profits will increase by $50,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If production is increased to 12,000 units, profits will increase by $100,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If production is remains at 10,000 units, profits will decrease by $50,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If production is remains at 10,000 units, profits will decrease by $100,000.

questions.explanation: Contribution margin falls from $85 - $50 = $35 to $85 - $60 = $25 once variable costs rise 20%. At 10,000 units, profit goes from (10,000 x $35) - $300,000 = $50,000 to (10,000 x $25) - $300,000 = -$50,000, a $100,000 decline. At 12,000 units profit would be exactly zero, still $50,000 worse than before, so raising output does not increase profit.
questions.explanationJa: 変動費が20%上昇すると、単位あたり貢献利益は $85 − $50 = $35 から $85 − $60 = $25 へ下がる。10,000単位のままなら利益は (10,000 × $35) − $300,000 = $50,000 から (10,000 × $25) − $300,000 = −$50,000 となり、$100,000 の悪化。12,000単位に増産しても利益はちょうどゼロで、従前より $50,000 悪いままなので、増産しても利益は増えない。

questions.stem: Break-even analysis assumes that over the relevant range
questions.explanation: Break-even analysis holds unit selling price and unit variable cost constant and treats total fixed cost as a horizontal line within the relevant range. That linearity is what allows a single break-even point to be computed; outside the relevant range the assumptions break down.
questions.explanationJa: 損益分岐点分析は、関連範囲内で単位あたり販売価格と単位あたり変動費を一定とし、固定費総額を水平な直線として扱う。この直線性があるからこそ損益分岐点を一点として計算できる。関連範囲を外れるとこれらの前提は成り立たなくなる。

questions.stem:
Wren Co. manufactures and sells two products with selling prices and variable costs as follows:
A | B
Selling price | $18.00 | $22.00
Variable costs | 12.00 | 14.00
Wren's total annual fixed costs are $38,400. Wren sells four units of A for every unit of B. If operating income last year was 28,800, what was the number of units Wren sold?
questions.explanation: Refer to the video explanation in the Proactive question bank (BAR CH52, Q.50, code 8892).
questions.explanationJa: 解説はProactive過去問解説の動画を参照（BAR CH52 / Q.50 / コード 8892）。

questions.stem: Bartlett Company is considering a new product, Pear. Bartlett's fixed costs are $200,000. Pear's contribution margin is $200 per unit. Bartlett has a marginal tax rate of 25%. How many units of Pear would Bartlett have to sell to have after-tax net income of $1,000,000?
questions.explanation: Work back from the after-tax target: pretax income = $1,000,000 / (1 - 25%) = $1,333,333. Total contribution margin needed = fixed costs $200,000 + $1,333,333 = $1,533,333. Units = $1,533,333 / $200 = 7,667. Using the after-tax figure directly would understate the requirement.
questions.explanationJa: 税引後の目標から逆算する。税引前利益 = $1,000,000 ÷ (1 − 25%) = $1,333,333。必要な貢献利益総額 = 固定費 $200,000 + $1,333,333 = $1,533,333。数量 = $1,533,333 ÷ $200 = 7,667単位。税引後の金額をそのまま使うと必要量を過小に見積もることになる。

questions.stem:
Rodder, Inc. manufactures a component in a router assembly. The selling price and unit cost data for the component are as follows.
Selling price | $15
Direct materials cost | 3
Direct labor cost | 3
Variable overhead cost | 3
Fixed manufacturing overhead cost | 2
Fixed selling and administration cost | 1
The company received a special one-time order for 1,000 components. Rodder has an alternative use for production capacity for the 1,000 components that would produce a contribution margin of $5,000.
What amount is the lowest unit price Rodder should accept for the component?
questions.explanation: The floor price covers incremental cost plus opportunity cost. Variable cost per unit = $3 + $3 + $3 = $9. Giving up the alternative use costs $5,000 / 1,000 units = $5 per unit. Minimum price = $9 + $5 = $14. Fixed manufacturing and selling costs are incurred regardless and are excluded.
questions.explanationJa: 最低価格は増分原価に機会費用を加えた水準となる。単位あたり変動費 = $3 + $3 + $3 = $9。代替用途を諦めることの費用は $5,000 ÷ 1,000単位 = $5/単位。最低価格 = $9 + $5 = $14。固定製造費用と固定販管費は受注の有無にかかわらず発生するため除外する。

questions.stem: Rice Co. plans to discontinue a department with a $24,000 contribution to overhead, and allocated overhead of $48,000, of which $21,000 cannot be eliminated. What would be the effect of this discontinuance on Rice's pretax profit?
questions.explanation: Discontinuing loses the $24,000 contribution but saves the overhead that can actually be eliminated: $48,000 - $21,000 = $27,000. Net effect = $27,000 - $24,000 = a $3,000 increase in pretax profit. The $21,000 that cannot be eliminated simply moves to other departments.
questions.explanationJa: 廃止すると貢献額 $24,000 を失うが、実際に削減できる間接費 $48,000 − $21,000 = $27,000 が節約できる。純効果 = $27,000 − $24,000 = 税引前利益の $3,000 増加。削減できない $21,000 は他部門へ振り替わるだけである。

questions.stem: Dale Company manufactures products Dee and Eff from a joint process. Product Dee has been allocated $5,000 of total joint costs of $40,000 for the 1,000 units produced. Dee can be sold at the split-off point for $6 per unit, or it can be processed further with additional costs of $2,000 and sold for $10 per unit. If Dee is processed further and sold, the result would be

choices.label: B
choices.text: An additional gain of $2,000 from further processing

choices.label: D
choices.text: An additional gain of $4,000 from further processing

questions.explanation: Joint costs of $5,000 are sunk and identical either way, so compare only what changes after split-off. Selling at split-off yields 1,000 x $6 = $6,000. Processing further yields 1,000 x $10 = $10,000 less the $2,000 of additional cost = $8,000. The gain from processing further is $2,000.
questions.explanationJa: 結合原価 $5,000 は埋没原価であり、どちらを選んでも同額なので、分離点より後で変化する部分だけを比較する。分離点で売却すると 1,000単位 × $6 = $6,000。追加加工すると 1,000単位 × $10 = $10,000 から追加費用 $2,000 を引いて $8,000。追加加工による利得は $2,000 となる。

questions.stem:
The manufacturing capacity of Gorb Company's facilities is 30,000 units of product a year. A summary of operating results for calendar Year 1 is as follows.
Sales (18,000 units @$50) | $900,000
Variable manufacturing and selling costs | (495,000)
Contribution margin | 405,000
Fixed costs | (247,500)
Operating income | $157,500
A foreign distributor has offered to buy 15,000 units at $45 per unit during Year 2. Assume that all of Gorb's costs would be at the same levels and rates in Year 2 as in Year 1. If Gorb accepted this offer and rejected some business from regular customers so as not to exceed capacity, what would be the total operating income for Year 2?
questions.explanation: Variable cost per unit = $495,000 / 18,000 = $27.50. Capacity is 30,000 units, so accepting 15,000 special units leaves room for only 15,000 regular units. Contribution = (15,000 x ($45 - $27.50)) + (15,000 x ($50 - $27.50)) = $262,500 + $337,500 = $600,000. Operating income = $600,000 - $247,500 = $352,500.

questions.stem:
Comel, Inc. has two major product lines: stoves and dryers. Comel's management wants to evaluate
whether discontinuing dryers will increase profits. Which of the following is best for evaluating the
discontinuance of the dryer product line?
questions.explanation: Discontinuance decisions turn on what actually changes if the line goes: the contribution lost and the costs genuinely avoided. That is the definition of relevant cost. Absorption cost includes allocated fixed overhead that will continue, which is precisely what makes a profitable line look unprofitable.
questions.explanationJa: 製品ラインを廃止する判断は、廃止した場合に実際に変化するもの、すなわち失われる貢献と本当に回避できる原価によって決まる。これが関連原価の定義である。全部原価には廃止後も発生し続ける配賦固定費が含まれており、それこそが採算の取れているラインを不採算に見せる原因となる。

questions.stem: At December 31, Caine Co. had a machine with an original cost of $104,000, accumulated depreciation of $70,000, and an estimated salvage value of zero. On December 31, Caine was considering the purchase of a new machine having a five-year life, costing $130,000, and having an estimated salvage value of $30,000 at the end of five years. In its decision concerning the possible purchase of the new machine, how much should Caine consider as sunk cost at December 31?
questions.explanation: Sunk cost is the amount already spent that no future decision can change: the old machine's book value of $104,000 - $70,000 = $34,000. The $130,000 price of the new machine and its $30,000 salvage value both lie in the future and are relevant to the decision.
questions.explanationJa: 埋没原価とは既に支出済みで、将来のいかなる決定によっても変えられない金額であり、旧機械の帳簿価額 $104,000 − $70,000 = $34,000 がこれにあたる。新機械の取得価額 $130,000 とその残存価額 $30,000 はいずれも将来の事象であり、意思決定に関連する数値である。

questions.stem:
Brent Co. has intracompany service transfers from Division Core, a cost center, to Division Pro, a profit center.
Under stable economic conditions, which of the following transfer prices is likely to be most conducive to evaluating whether both divisions have met their responsibilities?
questions.explanation: Transferring at standard variable cost keeps Core's own inefficiencies inside Core, since any excess over standard shows up as a variance in the cost center rather than being passed on. Pro is then charged only the cost that its demand genuinely causes, so each division is evaluated on what it controls. Actual cost would export Core's waste to Pro.
questions.explanationJa: 標準変動費で振り替えると、Core部門の非効率はCore部門の内部に留まる。標準を超えた分は原価センター側の差異として現れ、転嫁されないためである。Pro部門は自らの需要が本当に発生させた原価だけを負担するので、各部門は自分が管理できるものによって評価される。実際原価で振り替えるとCore部門の無駄がPro部門へ流出してしまう。

questions.stem:
Which of the following costing methods provide(s) the added benefit of usefulness for external reporting purposes?
I. Variable
II. Absorption
questions.explanation: US GAAP requires fixed manufacturing overhead to be inventoried, which only absorption costing does. Variable costing expenses that overhead immediately, so it is useful for internal decisions but cannot be used for external financial statements.
questions.explanationJa: 米国会計基準は固定製造間接費を棚卸資産に含めることを求めており、これを行うのは全部原価計算だけである。直接原価計算は当該間接費を直ちに費用処理するため、内部の意思決定には有用だが、外部向けの財務諸表には使えない。

questions.stem: Operating income using direct costing as compared to absorption costing would be higher

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the quantity to beginning inventory is less than the quantity of ending inventory

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the quantity to beginning inventory is more than the quantity of ending inventory

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the quantity to beginning inventory is equals the quantity of ending inventory

questions.explanation: Absorption costing defers fixed overhead in inventory. When inventory shrinks, the fixed cost stored in beginning inventory is released into expense on top of the current period's, so absorption income falls below variable costing income. That happens when beginning inventory exceeds ending inventory.
questions.explanationJa: 全部原価計算では固定間接費が在庫に繰り延べられる。在庫が減少する期には、期首在庫に含まれていた固定費が当期分に上乗せされて費用化されるため、全部原価計算の利益は直接原価計算を下回る。これは期首在庫が期末在庫を上回る場合に起こる。

questions.stem:
Sand Company has a calendar fiscal year and produces a single product that sells for $20 per unit. Sand uses an actual (historical) cost system. In the first year of operations, 100,000 units were produced and 80,000 units were sold. There was no work-in-process inventory at December 31. Manufacturing costs and selling and administrative expenses were as follows:
Fixed costs | Variable costs
Raw materials | -- | $4.00 per unit produced
Direct labor | -- | 2.50 per unit produced
Factory overhead | $240,000 | 1.50 per unit produced
Selling and administrative | 140,000 | 2.00 per unit sold
What is Sand's operating income under the variable (direct) costing method?
questions.explanation: Variable manufacturing cost = $4.00 + $2.50 + $1.50 = $8.00 per unit. Sales = 80,000 x $20 = $1,600,000. Variable costs of units sold = 80,000 x ($8.00 + $2.00 selling) = $800,000, so contribution margin = $800,000. Deduct all fixed costs of $240,000 + $140,000 = $380,000, giving operating income of $420,000.

questions.stem:
Sand Company has a calendar fiscal year and produces a single product that sells for $20 per unit. Sand uses an actual (historical) cost system. In the first year of operations, 100,000 units were produced and 80,000 units were sold. There was no work-in-process inventory at December 31. Manufacturing costs and selling and administrative expenses were as follows:
Fixed costs | Variable costs
Raw materials | -- | $4.00 per unit produced
Direct labor | -- | 2.50 per unit produced
Factory overhead | $240,000 | 1.50 per unit produced
Selling and administrative | 140,000 | 2.00 per unit sold
What is Sand's finished goods inventory at December 31, under the absorption costing method?
questions.explanation: Absorption costing adds fixed factory overhead to unit cost: $240,000 / 100,000 units produced = $2.40, so unit cost = $8.00 + $2.40 = $10.40. Ending inventory = 100,000 - 80,000 = 20,000 units x $10.40 = $208,000. Fixed selling costs are never inventoried under either method.
questions.explanationJa: 全部原価計算では固定製造間接費を単位原価に含める: $240,000 ÷ 生産量 100,000単位 = $2.40 なので、単位原価 = $8.00 + $2.40 = $10.40。期末在庫 = 100,000 − 80,000 = 20,000単位 × $10.40 = $208,000。固定販管費はどちらの方法でも棚卸資産に含めない。

questions.stem:
During May, Kern Co. produced and sold 10,000 units of a product. Manufacturing and selling costs incurred during May were as follows:
Direct materials and direct labor | $200,000
Variable manufacturing overhead | 45,000
Fixed manufacturing overhead | 10,000
Variable selling costs | 5,000
The product's unit cost under direct (variable) costing was
questions.explanation: Under direct costing the unit product cost includes only variable MANUFACTURING costs: ($200,000 + $45,000) / 10,000 = $24.50. Fixed manufacturing overhead is a period cost, and variable selling costs are never product costs under either method.
questions.explanationJa: 直接原価計算における単位製品原価には、変動「製造」原価だけを含める: ($200,000 + $45,000) ÷ 10,000単位 = $24.50。固定製造間接費は期間費用であり、変動販売費はいずれの方法でも製品原価にはならない。

questions.stem:
Cay Co.'s fixed manufacturing overhead costs totaled $100,000, and variable selling costs totaled $80,000. Under direct costing, how should these costs be classified?
Period costs | Product costs
questions.explanation: Direct costing treats fixed manufacturing overhead as a period cost, and selling costs are period costs regardless of behaviour. Both amounts are therefore expensed as incurred: $100,000 + $80,000 = $180,000 of period cost and nothing in product cost.
questions.explanationJa: 直接原価計算では固定製造間接費を期間費用として扱い、販売費は変動・固定を問わず期間費用である。したがって両方とも発生時に費用処理され、期間費用 $100,000 + $80,000 = $180,000、製品原価はゼロとなる。

questions.stem: Dowell Co. manufactures a wooden item. Which of the following is included with the inventoriable cost under absorption costing and excluded from the inventoriable cost under variable costing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cost of electricity used to operate production machinery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cost of scrap pieces of lumber

questions.explanation: The difference between the two methods is fixed manufacturing overhead, and straight-line depreciation on factory equipment is exactly that. Electricity to run machinery and assembly wages are variable manufacturing costs included under both methods, and scrap lumber is part of materials cost.
questions.explanationJa: 両方式の違いは固定製造間接費の扱いにあり、工場設備の定額法による減価償却費がまさにこれにあたる。機械を動かす電力費や組立工の賃金は変動製造原価であり、どちらの方式でも棚卸資産に含まれる。端材は材料費の一部である。

questions.stem: A manufacturing company prepares income statements using both absorption and variable costing methods. At the end of a period actual sales revenues, total gross profit, and total contribution margin approximated budgeted figures, whereas net income was substantially greater than the budgeted amount. There were no beginning or ending inventories. The most likely explanation of the net income increase is that, compared to budget, actual

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selling and administrative fixed expenses had decreased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sales prices and variable costs had increased proportionately.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sales prices had declined proportionately less than variable costs.

questions.explanation: Gross profit on budget means manufacturing costs behaved as planned; contribution margin on budget means variable costs did too. With revenue also on budget, the only remaining item that could lift net income is fixed selling and administrative expense, which must have come in below budget.
questions.explanationJa: 売上総利益が予算どおりであることは製造原価が計画どおりであったことを示し、貢献利益も予算どおりなら変動費も計画どおりだったことになる。売上高も予算どおりである以上、純利益を押し上げうる項目は固定販管費しか残らず、これが予算を下回ったと考えられる。

questions.stem:
Lynn Manufacturing Co. prepares income statements using both standard absorption and standard variable costing methods. For Year 2, unit standard cost were unchanged from Year 1. In Year 2, the only beginning and ending inventories were finished goods of 5,000 units. How would Lynn's ratios using absorption costing compare with those using variable costing?
Return on Current Ratio Stockholders' Equity
questions.explanation: Absorption costing carries fixed overhead in the 5,000 units of inventory, so inventory and thus current assets are larger, making the current ratio greater. That deferred cost also sits in retained earnings, so equity is larger while income is the same at equal beginning and ending inventories. A larger denominator with the same numerator makes return on equity smaller.
questions.explanationJa: 全部原価計算では在庫 5,000単位に固定間接費が含まれるため、棚卸資産ひいては流動資産が大きくなり、流動比率は高くなる。繰り延べられたその原価は利益剰余金にも残るので株主資本が大きくなる一方、期首と期末の在庫数量が等しいので利益は同額である。分子が同じで分母が大きくなるため、株主資本利益率は小さくなる。

questions.stem: At the end of a company's first year of operations, 2,000 units of inventory are on hand. Variable costs are $100 per unit, and fixed manufacturing costs are $30 per unit. The use of absorption costing, rather than variable costing, would result in a higher net income of what amount?
questions.explanation: In the first year there is no beginning inventory, so the entire fixed cost attached to ending inventory is the difference. Absorption costing defers 2,000 units x $30 = $60,000 of fixed manufacturing cost into inventory, while variable costing expenses it all, so absorption income is higher by $60,000. The $100 variable cost is inventoried under both methods.
questions.explanationJa: 初年度なので期首在庫がなく、期末在庫に付随する固定費の全額がそのまま差額となる。全部原価計算は 2,000単位 × $30 = $60,000 の固定製造費を在庫に繰り延べるのに対し、直接原価計算は全額を費用処理するため、全部原価計算の利益が $60,000 高くなる。変動費 $100 はどちらの方法でも棚卸資産に含まれる。

questions.stem: In an income statement prepared using the variable costing method, fixed factory overhead would

choices.label: B
choices.text: Be treated the same as variable factory overhead

choices.label: C
choices.text: Be used in the computation of operating income but not in the computation of the contribution margin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Be used in the computation of the contribution margin

questions.explanation: Contribution margin is sales less variable costs only, so fixed factory overhead is excluded from it. It is then deducted along with other fixed costs to arrive at operating income, which is why it appears in the statement but below the contribution margin line.
questions.explanationJa: 貢献利益は売上から変動費だけを差し引いて求めるため、固定製造間接費はそこに含まれない。その後、他の固定費とともに控除されて営業利益に至る。だからこの費用は損益計算書には現れるが、貢献利益より下の区分に位置する。

questions.stem:
Waldo Company, which produces only one product, provides its most current month's data as follows:
Selling price per unit | $80
Variable costs per unit:
Direct materials | 21
Direct labor | 10
Variable manufacturing overhead | 3
Variable selling and administrative | 6
Fixed costs:
Manufacturing overhead | $76,000
Selling and administrative | 58,000
Units:
Beginning inventory | 0
Month's production | 5,000
Number sold | 4,500
Ending inventory | 500
Based upon the above information, what is the total contribution margin for the month under the variable costing approach?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin is computed on units SOLD, not produced: 4,500 x $80 = $360,000 of sales. Variable cost per unit sold = $21 + $10 + $3 + $6 = $40, so $4,500 x $40 = $180,000. Contribution margin = $360,000 - $180,000 = $180,000. The 500 units in ending inventory carry variable manufacturing cost forward and do not affect this month's margin.
questions.explanationJa: 貢献利益は生産量ではなく「販売量」で計算する: 4,500単位 × $80 = 売上 $360,000。販売1単位あたりの変動費 = $21 + $10 + $3 + $6 = $40 なので、4,500 × $40 = $180,000。貢献利益 = $360,000 − $180,000 = $180,000。期末在庫 500単位は変動製造原価を翌月へ繰り越すだけで、当月の貢献利益には影響しない。

Asta, Inc., is a medical laboratory that performs tests for physicians. Asta anticipates performing between 5,000 and 12,000 tests during the month of April. Compared to industry averages, at the low range of activity Asta has a lower sales price per test, higher fixed costs, and the same break-even point in number of tests performed. At the high range of activity, Asta's sales price per test and fixed costs are the same as industry averages, and Asta's variable costs are lower. How is the office manager's salary categorized?

questions.stem: The CPA reviewed the minutes of a board of directors' meeting of LQR Corp., an audit client. An order for widget handles was outsourced to SDT Corp. because LQR couldn't fill the order. By having SDT produce the order, LQR was able to realize $100,000 in sales profits that otherwise would have been lost. The outsourcing added a cost of $10,000, but LQR was ahead by $90,000 when the order was completed. Which of the following statements is correct regarding LQR's action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The use of resource markets outside of LQR involves opportunity cost.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accounting profit is total revenue minus explicit costs and implicit costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implicit costs are not opportunity costs because they are internal costs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Explicit costs are opportunity costs from purchasing widget handles from resource market.

questions.explanation: Turning to an outside supplier is itself an economic choice: the resources bought there could have been obtained or deployed differently, so opportunity cost is inherent in using the resource market. Accounting profit deducts only explicit costs, and implicit costs are precisely the opportunity costs of resources the firm already owns, which makes B and C wrong as stated.
questions.explanationJa: 外部の供給者に頼ること自体が経済的な選択である。そこで購入する資源は別の方法で調達も配分もできたのだから、資源市場の利用には本質的に機会費用が伴う。会計上の利益は明示的費用のみを控除し、暗黙的費用とはまさに企業が既に保有する資源の機会費用であるため、BとCは記述として誤りである。

What amount should Augusta budget for cash payments to material suppliers during the period?
questions.explanation: Production is even, so weekly material use = 70,000 / 10 x $3 = $21,000. Payment lags one week, so the period's cash outflow covers the $40,000 opening payable plus weeks 1 through 9: $40,000 + (9 x $21,000) = $229,000. Week 10's usage is paid after the period ends.
questions.explanationJa: 生産は均等なので、1週間の材料使用額 = 70,000 ÷ 10週 × $3 = $21,000。支払は1週間遅れるため、期間中の現金支出は期首買掛金 $40,000 と第1週から第9週までの使用分を賄う: $40,000 + (9週 × $21,000) = $229,000。第10週の使用分は期間終了後に支払われる。

questions.stem: Of the following, which is the greatest disadvantage of direct (variable) costing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By expensing all fixed costs in the period incurred, the effects of fixed costs on net income are highlighted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: By expensing all fixed costs in the period incurred, record keeping is simplified.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Net income tends to vary with sales.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Egan Co. owns land that could be developed in the future. Egan estimates it can sell the land for $1,200,000, net of all selling costs. If it is not sold, Egan will continue with its plans to develop the land. As Egan evaluates its options for development or sale of the property, what type of cost would the potential selling price represent in Egan's decision?
questions.explanation: Choosing to develop means giving up the $1,200,000 the land could have been sold for, and a benefit forgone by taking one course over another is an opportunity cost. It is not sunk, since the sale is still available, and it is not a variable cost tied to activity.
questions.explanationJa: 開発を選ぶということは、土地を売却すれば得られた $1,200,000 を放棄することを意味し、ある選択をすることで放棄する便益は機会費用にあたる。売却の選択肢がまだ残っている以上、埋没原価ではなく、また操業度に連動する変動費でもない。

questions.stem: A delivery company is implementing a system to compare the costs of purchasing and operating different vehicles in its fleet. Truck 415 is driven 125,000 miles per year at a variable cost of $0.13 per mile. Truck 415 has a capacity of 28,000 pounds and delivers 250 full loads per year. What amount is the truck's delivery cost per pound?
questions.explanation: Annual variable cost = 125,000 miles x $0.13 = $16,250. Pounds carried = 28,000 pounds x 250 full loads = 7,000,000. Cost per pound = $16,250 / 7,000,000 = $0.00232. Dividing by loads rather than pounds would give $0.58 per load, not per pound.
questions.explanationJa: 年間変動費 = 125,000マイル × $0.13 = $16,250。年間輸送重量 = 28,000ポンド × 満載250回 = 7,000,000ポンド。1ポンドあたり原価 = $16,250 ÷ 7,000,000 = $0.00232。ポンド数ではなく積載回数で割ると $0.58 となるが、それは1回あたりの金額であってポンド単価ではない。
